title: Raw Pointers: References Without Rules
goal: Understand how raw pointers differ from references and where unsafe is required.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Raw Pointers

sections.text: In C or C++, pointers can point anywhere, be null, or alias freely. Rust references `&T` and `&mut T` guarantee safety at compile time, but raw pointers `*const T` and `*mut T` behave like C pointers.

sections.caption: Creating raw pointers from references is completely safe.

sections.text: Creating a raw pointer does not require `unsafe`. You can create null pointers or cast references to pointers anywhere in safe Rust code.
An `unsafe` block is required only when you dereference a raw pointer with `*ptr`. You promise the compiler that the pointer is non-null, aligned, and points to valid memory.

sections.caption: Dereferencing a raw pointer requires an unsafe block.

sections.text: Converting a raw pointer into a reference with `&*ptr` is dangerous. It asserts that all Rust reference rules hold, including aliasing and lifetime constraints.

explanation: Understand how raw pointers differ from references and where unsafe is required.
